note: A curated subset of MITRE ATT&CK mitigations (the M-series) relevant to an IoT honeypot, each mapped to generic attack family keys (see attack_families.json). This is the defensive / blue-team layer: it says what to DO about a detected attack, cited as [M####].

items.title: Password Policies
items.text: Set and enforce secure password policies for accounts: minimum length, complexity, no reuse of default or vendor passwords, and forced change on first use. Directly counters guessing and brute-force attempts against IoT devices that ship with weak defaults.

items.title: Multi-factor Authentication
items.text: Require more than one piece of evidence to authenticate, so a stolen or guessed password alone is not enough to gain access to management interfaces.

items.title: Account Use Policies
items.text: Configure account lockout, login attempt limits, and time-of-day restrictions. Rate-limiting and lockout make online brute-force attacks against a device impractical.

items.title: User Account Management
items.text: Manage the creation, modification, use, and permissions of accounts. Remove unused, shared, or backdoor accounts and grant each account only the access it needs.

items.title: Privileged Account Management
items.text: Manage privileged accounts and enforce least privilege, so that a compromised low-privilege account cannot reach administrative or critical functions.

items.title: Network Segmentation
items.text: Architect network segments to isolate IoT devices and critical systems, placing honeypot and production nodes behind separate boundaries so an intrusion or flood cannot spread laterally.

items.title: Network Intrusion Prevention
items.text: Use intrusion detection and prevention systems with signatures or anomaly rules to block malicious traffic in transit — scans, injection payloads, floods, and botnet command-and-control.

items.title: Filter Network Traffic
items.text: Filter inbound and outbound traffic with firewall and ACL rules: block spoofed source addresses, rate-limit floods, and deny traffic to known-bad or unexpected destinations to cut off exfiltration and C2.

items.title: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
items.text: Turn off or remove unneeded services, ports, and features to shrink the attack surface. An unused Telnet or debug service that is not running cannot be scanned, fingerprinted, or exploited.

items.title: Exploit Protection
items.text: Deploy exploit-mitigation capabilities (DEP, ASLR, stack protection, control-flow integrity) so that memory-corruption attempts crash safely or fail instead of yielding code execution.

items.title: Update Software
items.text: Keep firmware and software patched through a secure, signed update mechanism. Patching removes the known-vulnerable versions that scanners look for and that botnets exploit.

items.title: Encrypt Sensitive Information
items.text: Protect data in transit and at rest with strong encryption (e.g. TLS on every link). Encrypted traffic denies a man-in-the-middle the credentials and telemetry it would otherwise read or alter.

items.title: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
items.text: Restrict which hosts may reach a service over the network — bind management interfaces to the local network and allow-list known clients — so remote attackers cannot reach them at all.

items.title: Execution Prevention
items.text: Block execution of unauthorized code and scripts (application allow-listing, read-only firmware). Prevents uploaded web shells, injected commands, and dropped malware from running.

items.title: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
items.text: Use on-device controls that block behaviours associated with attacks — mass file encryption, suspicious process spawning — stopping ransomware and post-exploitation activity before it completes.

items.title: Antivirus/Antimalware
items.text: Run anti-malware that detects and quarantines known malicious code, including IoT botnet binaries and ransomware droppers, on the device or at the gateway.

items.title: Restrict Web-Based Content
items.text: Harden and restrict web content and input handling — output encoding, content security policy, disabling dangerous uploads — to neutralize cross-site scripting and malicious file uploads against device web interfaces.

items.title: Vulnerability Scanning
items.text: Scan your own devices and services to find weak, outdated, or misconfigured components before an attacker does, and feed the findings into patching and hardening.

items.title: Audit
items.text: Audit accounts, configurations, and permissions, and review logs for anomalies. Regular auditing surfaces backdoor accounts, unexpected open services, and signs of reconnaissance or exfiltration.

items.title: Software Configuration
items.text: Apply secure configuration to applications and services — parameterized queries, input validation, safe defaults — to close the injection and scripting weaknesses that attackers target.
